findings.title: Different-policy reconciliation falsely announces that the prior setting remains active
findings.reproduction: At candidate b079bdd68e648d8059b64b984eaa841059312fe0, the table-driven case in apps/desktop/src/app/applicationSettings.test.ts:219 prepares windows-password profile Requested with timeout 60 from profile Prior/timeout 15/revision 2, loses both commit and receipt-replay responses, observes revision 3 with either profile Other or timeout 0, and receives a successful cancellation/cleanup receipt. The test asserts the returned different snapshot with kind unchanged at line 262. ApplicationSettingsController.reconcileInterruptedCommit reaches apps/desktop/src/app/applicationSettings.ts:393-394 and says native status confirms the prior setting remains active. That statement is false because the returned snapshot is revision 3 and differs from the prior revision-2 policy; in the timeout fixture protection has materially fallen from 15/60 intent to zero. ApplicationSettingsWorkspace.applyResult applies every returned snapshot and then emits that contradictory message through the live region. Thus the remediation correctly prevents a saved/success claim but does not provide the conflict/uncertain report explicitly required by R01, and a screen-reader user is told the opposite of the policy now projected on the page.
findings.required_remediation: When exact-target receipt/status reconciliation fails and the observed native snapshot differs from the prepared source, preserve that observed snapshot for truthful current-state display but return a rejected/conflict-style result whose plain-language message states that the policy changed elsewhere, the requested transition was not confirmed, and the user must review or refresh before retrying. Do not label this path unchanged or state that the prior policy remains active. Keep bounded cancellation cleanup. Update both wrong-profile and wrong-timeout controller fixtures to assert the conflict result and message, and add or extend one workspace interaction assertion proving the contradictory success/unchanged live announcement cannot occur.

closures.evidence: The high-risk core exploit is fixed: complete normalized target plus exact successor revision are retained, opaque-handle receipt replay is preferred, direct and recovered receipts are validated, and independent replay confirms wrong-profile and wrong-timeout same-mode status cannot produce committed or reconciled-committed success. W1.A05.T04-R02-F01 narrowly retains the unresolved truthful conflict-announcement portion of the original required remediation; it does not reopen the false-success authority claim.

The previous guided workspace remains mounted inside a hidden, aria-hidden, inert layer while Application Settings is active. Independent built-product replay created and opened a project, changed the Research Intent use case and objective without saving, opened settings, returned, and retained the exact project, workspace, field values, and intended top-bar focus.

Locked recovery places all background content in an inert and aria-hidden subtree, the global handler suppresses Ctrl+K, Ctrl+/, and Alt+H while confirmation is active, focus stays inside the alertdialog, and no deferred dialog appears after unlock. Application Settings captures the actual top-bar, sidebar, or command-result element and independently restores all three connected initiators with a stable fallback. The built-product replay and full workflow/accessibility/visual conformance matrix passed.
